answers.deadlock_strong: A deadlock is when two or more processes wait for each other forever, so none of them can continue. It needs four conditions at the same time: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. For example, process P1 holds a printer and waits for the scanner, while P2 holds the scanner and waits for the printer. We can prevent it by breaking one condition, for example always requesting resources in a fixed order, or avoid it with the Banker's algorithm. Detection plus recovery is also possible, but killing processes has a cost.
answers.proc_partial: A process is a program in execution and a thread is a part of a process. Threads are lighter than processes.
answers.proc_polished: A process is a program in execution that has its own separate memory space. A thread is a smaller unit of execution inside a process, and all threads of a process share that memory. Because of this, creating and switching threads is cheaper than processes. For example, Chrome runs each tab as a separate process, while a game uses separate threads for rendering and sound.
